acceptance: All SDKs pass the same compatibility test suite.
verifiedBy: cargo fmt --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --all -- --check && cargo test --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --workspace && pnpm test

demonstration.sharedFixtures: All three clients are tested against the identical canonical v1 golden envelopes and the identical closed error-code index, not independently authored equivalents: operations/operations/membrane-context.v1.golden.json, membrane-context.v1.error.golden.json, membrane-source-read.v1.golden.json, membrane-source-read.v1.error.golden.json, and operations-index.v1.golden.json.
demonstration.rust: engine/crates/membrane-client/tests/compat.rs (new in this task) loads those five fixtures directly and asserts: golden success data extraction for membrane_context and membrane_source_read; golden error typing (context_deadline_exceeded/retryable=true, source_read_hash_mismatch/retryable=false); every error code listed in operations-index.v1.golden.json for both operations round-trips as a typed ProtocolError; an error code outside that index, a schemaVersion drift, a response-operation mismatch, an unknown top-level field, and an unsupported operation all fail closed with the correct protocol_* code.
demonstration.typescript: tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs (pre-existing, re-verified unmodified and passing in this task) asserts the same golden envelopes' schemaVersion/errorVersion/operation, that the TypeScript client accepts golden success and types golden error identically, that every operations-index error code for both operations is present and correctly typed by the TypeScript, Python, and Rust source, and that version drift is rejected.
demonstration.python: tests/sdk/python_client_test.py's pre-existing PythonClientTest class (unmodified) plus the new PythonClientGoldenFixtureTest class (added in this task) load the same five fixtures directly and assert the same success-extraction, typed-and-retryable error, every-indexed-error-code, and fail-closed behaviors as the Rust and TypeScript suites.
demonstration.mechanicalSchemaCheck: The error-code sets each client accepts are asserted against operations-index.v1.golden.json's errorCodes arrays (loaded at test time in all three languages) rather than hand-copied into the tests, and tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs additionally asserts every golden envelope's schemaVersion/errorVersion/operation against the ENVELOPE_VERSION/ERROR_VERSION/*_OPERATION constants exported by the TypeScript client — so a change to the shared schema or index that a client's closed-field/closed-error-code validation does not track fails a test instead of requiring review to notice.
demonstration.transportRealityCheck: docs/sdk/http-transport.md (new) and tests/sdk/http-transport-contract.test.mjs (new) tie the SDK documentation for wiring an HTTP transport to the literal path/header constants in engine/crates/membrane-runtime/src/mcp_http.rs (MBR-306) and the literal denial-code enum in schemas/http-mcp-security.v1.schema.json, read at test time so a rename in the real transport source fails the doc check mechanically. The same document states, based on reading engine/crates/membrane-mcp/src/jsonrpc.rs, that the shared dispatcher's tools/call branch is currently a stub for every tool call over any transport, so no SDK claims a working live HTTP round trip today — only the golden-fixture and directly-injected-transport paths this evidence demonstrates.
